verdicts.note: Chapter on the AGE at which young people gain rights to basic income and to housing. That is scope §4 design 1 and design 6 stated as policy architecture; worth reading for which thresholds exist to exploit.
KIDS COUNT data portal record.
Role conflict and social support among married Taiwanese childcare workers in continuing education.

Leaving home, rights to support and EMANCIPATION as a legal category. The legal-threshold literature behind design 6; note that this is the sense in which 'emancipation' is used here, which is neither the Spanish residential sense nor the political one.
Causal effect of the NUMBER OF CHILDREN on elderly parents' health in China. Reverse direction and a health outcome; C.3.c's old-age-security question.

Relationship dynamics between wives and their HUSBANDS' FAMILIES and their interconnection with childbearing behaviour in rural Nepal, explicitly against the thin empirical base on extended-family systems. Directly on the extended arm's estimand.
European welfare systems viewed through life-stage transitions.
Review essay on Therborn and Thornton; developmental idealism. D.1.b's.

Gated anchor. Nationally representative surveys of married women in JAPAN AND ITALY, arguing that explanations of very low fertility in strong-family countries emphasise childrearing costs and ignore the offsetting influence of DISTINCTIVE LIVING ARRANGEMENTS. The proximity cell's core record, and it spans the two settings the two arms live in.

Grandparent-PROVIDED CHILD CARE against fertility intentions in Italy, framed through familism. Under the 222/223 ruling the exposure is the grandparent's time rather than the living arrangement, so it routes to C.2.a -- but the familism framing and the Italian setting make it a boundary case worth reading with the extended arm.
Encyclopedia entry on family development theory.
Self-perceived health among older adults in India.
Editorial introduction to a Future of Children issue on coming of age.
Children's accounts of parental drug use.

'Emptying the Nest': the share of married men 60+ living only with their wives rose from 19% to 78% between 1880 and 2000, most of it between 1940 and 1970. The exposure trend measured from the PARENTS' side over 120 years of US census data.
Commentary on Australian tax-transfer review.
RESIDENTIAL INDEPENDENCE and other adult role markers against contact with grandparents. Arrangement as exposure, kin contact as outcome.
No abstract; parental divorce effects on children in a European case.
Husbands' labour migration and wives' decision-making autonomy in Mozambique. Spousal separation is A.14's, not the parental arrangement.
Book review, Japanese death rites.
Qualitative study of new parents' relationships with the new grandparents.
No abstract; mental health among older married couples.
No abstract; social outcomes in young adult cancer survivors.

Commentary arguing that most natural-fertility studies do NOT support the grandmother hypothesis. A negative result on the evolutionary premise the extended arm's kin-support literature rests on; theory, no arrangement exposure.
Intergenerational congruence in family attitudes by life-course stage.
No abstract; post-stroke discharge destination.

'How Grandparents Matter': kin support as the route by which women combine work and motherhood, against the formal-childcare focus of demography. Exposure is kin availability rather than the arrangement, so C.2.a's under the ruling; the cooperative-breeding framing is the extended arm's theoretical backbone.
Ethics case on sexuality after severe brain injury.
Priests' influence on Dutch Catholic family size. D.1.a's secularisation question.

Explicitly studies THE FULL SEQUENCE FROM LIVING IN THE PARENTAL HOME TO A FIRST BIRTH rather than the final transition alone, in three pre-transitional European communities. That is §3's joint-determination problem taken as the unit of analysis. Pre-modern, so A.7's under Ruling 2, but methodologically the closest thing in the frame to what §3 asks for. Priority read.
Psychological practice for missing-children cases in Brazil.

Influence of MOTHERS-IN-LAW on young couples' family planning decisions in rural India, in patrilocal households, examining how intra-family relations shape contraceptive method and timing. The extended arm's mechanism at the decision level.
Neighbourhood life-history variation in England; expected reproductive lifespan as the exposure.
Son preference in patrilineal, patrilocal Nepal. D.2.c's.

Furstenberg's 'On a New Schedule' -- a gated anchor and the nearest thing this literature has to a review, on the extended timetable for entering adulthood and the family life of young adults and their parents.
Fertility history and later-life quality of life.
Household structure and food insecurity. Arrangement as exposure, food security as outcome.
Membership hierarchies for foreigners in Korea.
Duplicate of the preceding Korean membership article.

'Italians Are Late': whether a late transition to adulthood reduces lifetime economic opportunity, with Italy's near-lowest fertility as the framing. The registered hypothesis's setting, with the economic rather than the autonomy mechanism.
Personality and work-family conflict.
Self-perceived health of older adults in India; companion to the earlier record.
Street-based child workers in India.
Life satisfaction among women in Korean multicultural families.
Statistical release on married couples with children living at home, 1996.
Companion release, married couples with no children living at home.
Orange County voter attitudes poll.
Young Pakistani women's preparedness for reproductive life.
Film review, women in hip hop.
Parent-offspring conflict theory applied to family relationships.
No abstract; POSTMARITAL RESIDENCE dynamics among the Hadza. A residence-rule exposure in a forager population; outcome not visible.
Depression among pregnant women testing for HIV in South Africa.
Marriage attitudes, intentions and perceived barriers in Japan. A.7's.
Medical school dropout prediction.
Korean residents' awareness of family-friendly policy.
